en: Itivuttaka 10: Ekakanipāta, First Chapter Thus it was said. In this connection, the Blessed One spoke as follows: "Monks, there is one thing which, if cultivated and made much of, leads to the complete destruction of suffering. What is that one thing? It is equanimity (*upekkhā*). Monks, this one thing, if cultivated and made much of, leads to the complete destruction of suffering. Thus spoke the Blessed One. Having said this, the Well-Farer rose from his seat and entered his dwelling. Then, not long after the Blessed One had departed, a certain monk approached the Venerable Ānanda and said to him: "Friend Ānanda, what is the meaning of this statement spoken by the Blessed One: 'Monks, there is one thing which, if cultivated and made much of, leads to the complete destruction of suffering. What is that one thing? It is equanimity. Monks, this one thing, if cultivated and made much of, leads to the complete destruction of suffering'? "It is wonderful, friend, it is marvelous! How well has the Dhamma been taught by the Blessed One, who knows and sees, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Enlightened One. For the Blessed One has declared: 'Monks, there is one thing which, if cultivated and made much of, leads to the complete destruction of suffering. What is that one thing? It is equanimity. Monks, this one thing, if cultivated and made much of, leads to the complete destruction of suffering. And how, friend, is equanimity cultivated and made much of so that it leads to the complete destruction of suffering? Here, friend, a monk dwells contemplating the body in the body, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure regarding the world. He dwells contemplating feelings in feelings... mind in the mind... phenomena in phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, and mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure regarding the world. It is in this way, friend, that equanimity is cultivated and made much of so that it leads to the complete destruction of suffering. When the Venerable Ānanda had spoken thus, that monk said to the Venerable Ānanda: "It is wonderful, friend, it is marvelous! How well has the Dhamma been taught by the Blessed One, who knows and sees, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Enlightened One. For the Blessed One has declared: 'Monks, there is one thing which, if cultivated and made much of, leads to the complete destruction of suffering. What is that one thing? It is equanimity. Monks, this one thing, if cultivated and made much of, leads to the complete destruction of suffering. Thus it was said. In this connection, the Blessed One spoke as follows: "Monks, there is one thing which, if cultivated and made much of, leads to the complete destruction of suffering. What is that one thing? It is equanimity. Monks, this one thing, if cultivated and made much of, leads to the complete destruction of suffering. Thus spoke the Blessed One. Having said this, the Well-Farer rose from his seat and entered his dwelling. And that is how this discourse was spoken by the Blessed One; having heard it, the monks held it in mind.
The Discourse on the Full Understanding of Hatred.
This was said by the Blessed One, said by the Arahant; thus have I heard:

"Bhikkhus, one who does not directly know hatred, does not fully understand it, and does not cause the mind to become dispassionate toward it or abandon it, is incapable of the destruction of suffering."
"But by directly knowing and fully understanding aversion, bhikkhus, and by detaching the mind from it and abandoning it, one is capable of the destruction of suffering.
Thus the Blessed One spoke. With reference to this, it is said:
“Having fully understood that hatred by which beings, corrupted by hatred, go to an evil destination— ”
Those who possess insight abandon them;
having abandoned them, they never again return to this world.
This matter too was spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
Furthermore, from pride arise both lust and hatred;
these two are proclaimed as the first group.
